items.title: Regex for Beginners: Find Anything in Text (Python Regular Expressions Tutorial)
items.description:
Learn regular expressions (regex) in Python from zero: find every phone number, email address and date in any text with one short pattern. Step by step for complete beginners, with re.findall, groups, re.sub and re.fullmatch, plus the three mistakes everyone makes. Every output on screen is the real result of the code shown.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:33 Find vs. regex
0:52 The plan
1:07 Setup
1:24 Step 1: your first pattern
2:14 The building blocks
2:37 Step 2: find phone numbers
3:16 Step 3: find email addresses
4:07 Step 4: groups
4:48 Step 5: hide numbers with re.sub
5:35 Step 6: is this code valid?
6:11 Mistake 1: greedy matches
6:38 Mistake 2: forgetting the r
6:55 Mistake 3: the dot and brackets
7:14 Pro tip: ignore upper and lower case
7:45 Recap

Practice text (inbox.txt, all fictional)
From: Maria Lopez (maria.lopez@sunnybakery.com)
Order 4417 arrived on 2026-10-03. Please call 555-201-7788.
From: Tom Reyes (tom_r@greenleaf.cafe)
Invoice 1042 is late. My number is 555-318-9020.
From: Dana Kim (dana.kim+orders@brightdental.org)
Meeting moved to 2026-11-20. Office line: 555-404-1234.

phones.py (find every phone number)
import re

text = open("inbox.txt").read()

phones = re.findall(r"\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}", text)
print(phones)
print(len(phones), "phone numbers")

emails.py (find every email address)
import re

text = open("inbox.txt").read()

emails = re.findall(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.\w+", text)
for email in emails:
    print(email)

dates.py (groups: year, month, day)
import re

text = open("inbox.txt").read()

for year, month, day in re.findall(r"(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})", text):
    print(f"{day}/{month}/{year}")

hide.py (mask phone numbers with re.sub)
import re

text = open("inbox.txt").read()

safe = re.sub(r"\d{3}-\d{3}-(\d{4})", r"XXX-XXX-\1", text)
print(safe)

check.py (validate a code with re.fullmatch)
import re

codes = ["AB-1234", "ab-1234", "AB-12345", "XAB-1234"]

for code in codes:
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Z]{2}-\d{4}", code):
        print(code, "valid")
    else:
        print(code, "invalid")

Regex cheat sheet
\d digit  |  \w letter, digit or _  |  \s space  |  . any character
+ one or more  |  * zero or more  |  ? optional  |  {3} exactly 3  |  [abc] one of a, b, c
( ) group  |  .*? lazy (stops early)  |  \. a real dot

Common problems:
One giant match instead of several  -  .* is greedy, use .*? instead
Empty list, no error  -  you forgot the r before the quotes (raw string)
Dot matches too much  -  escape it: \.
re.error: missing ), unterminated subpattern  -  a round bracket was never closed
Nothing found because of capital letters  -  add re.IGNORECASE
